exercises.depth_review: The changed combined uncertainty, each solved safety inequality, validity of the boundary measurement and distinction between sufficient-certificate failure and actual impossibility are explained.

The sufficient interval has ordered endpoints, lower endpoint <=1 and upper endpoint >=-1, proving nonempty actuator intersection. Boundary states demand incompatible constant-input inequalities.

The true-safe-set optimization is correctly conditional on additional performance information.

exercises.mathematics_review: A zero global Lipschitz constant forces equality of all function values. A lower margin 0.16 transfers to every point. If the only available information is a negative lower bound, the lower-bound test certifies nothing and does not prove negativity of the constant; division by zero is avoided.

exercises.depth_review: Each unit conversion and coefficient substitution is shown; the bound is attained, so the strict certificate genuinely fails. The answer explains why changing the uncertainty set or metric without conversion changes the question.

exercises.mathematics_review: ceil(20*0.99)=20 exceeds 19 finite ranks. The augmented infinity convention gives a vacuous residual set. The exchangeable continuous no-tie counterexample has calibration-maximum coverage 19/20=0.95, so clipping cannot inherit a distribution-free 0.99 guarantee.
exercises.depth_review: The unavailable order statistic, conservative construction and interpretation are explicit. Uniform test-score rank gives a complete concrete reason for the failure of silent clipping, rather than a bare caution.

exercises.mathematics_review: Union failure is at most 0.4, hence success at least 0.6. Under mutual independence the product lower bound is 0.9^4=0.6561; equality requires all marginal success probabilities to be 0.9. Per-prediction failure <=0.025 yields joint failure <=0.1.
exercises.depth_review: Failure events, union and complement are defined; each probability substitution and the independence condition are shown. The final calibration qualification correctly prevents an allocated budget from being mistaken for an achieved guarantee.
